newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG AND LIVERPOOL SEEK TO KEEP TROPHY HOPES ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG AND LIVERPOOL SEEK TO KEEP TROPHY HOPES ALIVE.

text.p: Holders Paris St Germain and Liverpool battle it out in a Cup Winners Cup semifinal first leg at the Parc des Princes on Thursday knowing defeat in the tie will largely end their season's hopes.
Both will be trying to bounce back after disastrous league performances in recent weeks.

A 1-1 draw at home against lowly Rennes left PSG trailing Monaco by 12 points in the French league standings and the team coached by Brazil's Ricardo look set to finish second for the third year running.
Meanwhile Liverpool wasted a golden opportunity to go top of the English premier league by losing at home 2-1 to lowly Coventry.

Paris St Germain are bidding to become the first side to retain the Cupwinners Cup, the only European competition they have won, while Liverpool are seeking the only continental trophy to have eluded them.
"We realise we could finish with nothing this season," said Liverpool's veteran skipper John Barnes.
"We don't want to finish empty-handed, It will be a big disappointment if we don't win something."
But while Liverpool still have some chance of winning the English championship, PSG's league hopes are in tatters.
"The Cupwinners Cup is our last hope to shine this season. Everybody's aware of it," said midfielder Jerome Leroy.
Paris St Germain will be playing in their fifth consecutive semifinal of a European competition. After three failures, they at last won the Cup Winners Cup last season.
Liverpool have won almost everything on offer in Europe -- four European Cups and two UEFA Cups -- and they beat the two French sides they have met in past competitions, St Etienne and Auxerre.
PSG, on the other hand, were ousted by Arsenal at this stage in 1994.
"We're not favourites. Liverpool are a much better team than Arsenal were three years ago," said PSG president Michel Denisot.
But Barnes also expressed a lot of respect for the Parisians.
"I would rate PSG along with Monaco, who beat Newcastle in both legs of the UEFA Cup. Monaco are probably a bit more fluent, PSG probably a bit stronger," he said.
Both teams should be able to count on full squads.
Brazil's Leonardo and defender Bruno N'Gotty return from injury for PSG while Liverpool defender Mark Wright is back from suspension for Liverpool.
As for tactics, they sound fairly simple.
"Our aim must be to win both ties," said Barnes.
"Our aim must be not to concede goals," said PSG coach Ricardo, adding that PSG lost in the semifinals each time they conceded a goal at home.
Teams (probable):
Paris St Germain - 1-Bernard Lama; 22-Didier Domi, 6-Paul Le Guen, 4-Bruno N'Gotty, 13-Laurent Fournier; 15-Benoit Cauet, 8-Vincent Guerin, 19-Jerome Leroy; 10-Rai, 7-Leonardo, 11-Patrice Loko.

Liverpool - 1-David James; 21-Dominic Matteo, 5-Mark Wright, 12-Steve Harkness, 4-Jason McAteer; 20-Stig-Inge Bjornebye, 11-Jamie Redknapp, 10-John Barnes; 7-Steve McManaman, 8-Stan Collymore, 9-Robbie Fowler.
